title: Oncall autograder and playbook-deviation detector
author: Priya Shah
release_notes: Add on-call action scoring and playbook-deviation detector. Feature gated, opt-in for orgs. Improves incident postmortems and surfaces automation candidates.
content:
Context and motivation:
We frequently see flights where responders take ad-hoc actions that drift from the canonical playbook. That drift increases MTTR variance and hides repeatable automation opportunities. This PR introduces an "autograder" that scores on-call actions against the canonical playbook guidance and a playbook-deviation detector that flags incidents where the deviation pattern crosses a threshold. The goal is to make deviations visible, provide seed feedback to runbook authors, and enable safe automation recommendations without changing any on-call workflow by default.

What this PR does (summary):
- Adds an action-scoring pipeline in incident-bot that consumes telemetry checkpoints (commands run, timeline events, console outputs, key alerts acknowledged) and computes a normalized 'alignment' score against the recommended playbook steps.
- Adds a playbook-deviation detector that computes per-incident deviation profiles (sequence-level and step-level) and emits signals when deviation rate or semantic divergence exceeds tunable thresholds.
- Stores checkpointed graded snapshots (hashed) for auditing and human-in-the-loop review; no PII is stored — sanitized fields only.
- Exposes a lightweight API and a console view (feature flag) for SRE leads to inspect high-deviation incidents and suggested playbook edits.
- Implements a safe rollout: feature-gated, org opt-in, and initially read-only (no automated remediations).

Design notes and tradeoffs:
- Scoring model: rule-backed heuristic with a small trained ranker (ensemble). The heuristics cover timing, step presence, and argument similarity; the ranker helps disambiguate semantically-similar freeform actions. We deliberately avoided a fully opaque ML policy for the first rollout to keep auditability high.
- Telemetry checkpoints: checkpoints are sampled at step boundaries to keep cost manageable; we also provide a high-fidelity sampling mode behind a separate flag for pilot orgs.
- Privacy and safety: explicit sanitizers applied to CLI outputs and snippets; only feature-flagged orgs will have graded snapshots persisted. All persisted artifacts are hashed and linked to incident IDs for audit.

Implementation details (files changed, high level):
- incident-bot/pkg/autograder/*: scoring engine, heuristics, ranker wrapper (GO).
- incident-bot/api/v1/autograder.go: new HTTP endpoints (POST /autograder/score, GET /autograder/incident/{id}).
- incident-bot/web/console/autograder-panel: read-only UI with deviation timeline and example action snippets.
- incident-bot/cmd/checkpoint-agent: small change to include graded metadata in checkpoint envelope.
- infra/k8s/incident-bot-configmap.yaml: feature flag defaults and sampling params.
- test/*_autograder_test.go: unit tests and a small end-to-end fixture that replays synthetic incidents.

Commits (high level):
- feat: initial scoring pipeline and heuristics (3 commits)
- feat: ranker integration and unit tests (2 commits)
- feat: API + console view + feature flag (2 commits)
- chore: sampling knobs, config, and docs (1 commit)
- test: add e2e replay fixture and CI flake fixes (1 commit)

Testing and CI notes:
- CI initially showed a flaky e2e replay test on Linux macOS matrix (repro: timing-dependent assertion). Fixed by switching to event-driven assertions in tests. All checks green on final runs.
- Integration smoke: deployed to staging incident-bot with the autograder flag enabled for the "eng-sre" org only. Observed no detectable increase in CPU at the pod level when sampling rate was 5%.

Metrics and monitoring introduced:
- autograder.alignment_score.p50/p95 (histogram)
- autograder.deviation_incidents.count (counter, per-org)
- autograder.storage.bytes (gauge)
- autograder.latency.p99 (histogram)
- Console: deviation incidents list with links to sanitized checkpoints

Rollout plan and gate control:
1) Canary: stage for 'eng-sre' org with sampling=5% (2 days) — done in staging.
2) Pilot: enable for opt-in beta orgs (feature flag) with sampling up to 20% and UI enabled for SRE leads (1 week).
3) General availability: roll to any org via console opt-in and default sampling 1%.
Feature toggles implemented via configmap and dynamic refresh; we also added an org-level opt-in switch in the console.

Migration and data: none required. Existing incident checkpoints are compatible. Storages are on a new table incident_autograde_snapshots with TTL default 90 days.

Review conversation (high-level):
- Ethan Cole: "This looks promising. Two asks: (1) add an audit trail for any score changes after manual review, (2) ensure we can turn sampling down without redeploy."
- Priya (author): "Added score_change_audit table and implemented dynamic sampling via ConfigMap refresh. See commit feat: add audit trail + dynamic sampling (hash: a12b3c)."
- Marta Ivanova: "Can we redact more CLI arg content by default? I worry about accidental secrets in snapshots."
- Priya: "Expanded the sanitizer list and added a conservative redact-first policy. Sanitation test cases added to test suite."
- Jun Park: "Approach seems fine; please ensure UI is read-only initially and that no automations are wired to the detector yet."
- Priya: "Confirmed — UI is read-only and webhooks for automation exist but remain disabled behind 'auto_recommendations' flag (off by default)."
- Approval flow: Ethan gave LGTM after audit trail added; Marta approved after sanitizer uplifts; Jun gave final approval.

Operational concerns and mitigations:
- Cost: snapshot storage controlled by sampling + TTL; added autograder.storage.bytes gauge and alert at 1GB/week per org.
- False positives: detector emits an initial 'suspect' state; human review is required to mark as 'confirmed deviation' for learning dataset ingestion.
- Abuse: access to graded snapshots gated to org admins and SRE leads only; toggles require owner-level to flip.

Follow-ups and next steps:
- ENG-4199: pipeline to convert confirmed deviations into suggested playbook diffs for authors (separate PR).
- Experiment: run A/B on sentinel suggestions vs no suggestions to measure MTTR improvement.
- Longer-term: investigate replacing the ranker with a small explainable transformer if we can ship more rigorous audits.

Merge outcome:
- Merged via squash on 2026-03-04 after required approvals. Release notes added.

Notes for reviewers and ops: this PR intentionally keeps the first iteration read-only and opt-in. Please coordinate with Security for any org pilot that wants to enable higher sampling rates.
